objective: Fix the source-capability UI so the seven restricted boards no longer show stale, pre-search-provider wording ('Automated discovery not authorized' etc.) once a search provider makes them usable -- aggregate direct-source capability + search-provider capability into one board-level capability record and wire the GUI to actually use it.
root_cause: scripts/source_capabilities.py already computed final_status/search_provider_status/search_provider_active_provider fields (built in the prior Phase 14.2 turn), but web/app.js's renderSourceStatus()/shortReason() were never updated to read them -- they still rendered the raw, pre-Phase-14 `reason` investigation text via a hardcoded lookup table (NOT_AUTHORIZED -> 'Automated access not authorized', etc.), which is exactly the stale wording the screenshot showed. The backend had the right data; the frontend was ignoring it.
live_activation_note: Search-provider architecture ready; no provider key configured.

INDEED.quality_note: Indeed's own search-result titles never include a company name -- preserved as a separate note, not a status downgrade.

restricted_boards_available_through_sear: None right now -- no provider key is configured in this environment. Verified via an isolated test server with a placeholder SERPER_API_KEY that ALL SEVEN restricted boards correctly flip to final_status=AVAILABLE_VIA_SEARCH_PROVIDER, search_provider='SERPER', and move into the GUI's Available bucket the instant a provider becomes eligible -- see verification_evidence below.

unavailable_boards_and_reason.note: No board is 'unavailable' in the sense of being impossible -- every restricted board's real reason is documented separately (direct_status=NOT_AUTHORIZED, from Phase 12/13's dated robots.txt/anti-bot evidence) and every one offers manual_import_available=true as a fallback regardless of provider configuration.

failover_behavior: Unchanged from the prior Phase 14.2 turn: SearchProviderManager tries providers in priority order (default you -> tavily -> exa -> brave -> serper), skips unconfigured/disabled/over-budget providers, returns immediately on any successful call (including an empty result list -- never treated as failure), and moves to the next provider on QUOTA_EXHAUSTED/AUTH_FAILED/RATE_LIMITED (after that provider's own internal retry loop)/SERVER_ERROR. Raises SearchProviderPoolExhausted (never a fabricated result) if every eligible provider fails or none is configured. Not re-tested this turn beyond confirming it still passes unchanged (this turn's changes were capability-model/GUI only).

verification_evidence.live_api_check_unconfigured: GET /api/sources against the real (shared) dev server confirmed every restricted board's final_status now reads SEARCH_PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED and direct_status reads NOT_AUTHORIZED -- no stale ENABLED_DIRECT claim, no stale 'Automated discovery not authorized' text.
verification_evidence.live_api_check_configured: A short-lived, isolated uvicorn instance with a placeholder SERPER_API_KEY confirmed LINKEDIN's capability record exactly matches this phase's own Part 16 API example: {source_provider: 'SERPER', final_status: 'AVAILABLE_VIA_SEARCH_PROVIDER', direct_status: 'NOT_AUTHORIZED'}.
verification_evidence.real_browser_check_unconfigured: A real Chromium (Playwright) session against the dashboard's Sources card showed: 'CUTSHORT — Search provider not configured / Configure a search API to enable discovery. / Import a job manually' for every restricted board -- the exact replacement wording for the screenshot's stale text.
verification_evidence.real_browser_check_configured: The same check against the isolated, placeholder-key server showed all seven restricted boards move into the 'Available' section as '✓ LINKEDIN — Search Provider: Serper', plus a new 'Search Provider Status: 1 provider configured · Automatic failover: ON' line.
verification_evidence.checkbox_routing_check: New Search's checkbox list (searches/new) was confirmed, via the same real browser session, to show the friendly label 'LINKEDIN (via Search Provider: Serper)' while submitting the correct internal value 'LINKEDIN_SEARCH' -- and a real POST to /api/candidates/{id}/searches with sources=['LINKEDIN_SEARCH','NAUKRI'] was accepted (200). The test search row created during this manual check was archived immediately afterward.

modified_files: scripts/source_capabilities.py (board-level final_status priority logic exactly matching Part 4; new direct_status/search_provider/source fields matching Part 16's exact API shape; search_provider_status/final_status now derived from the SAME live is_provider_configured() check as search_provider_active_provider, fixing a real inconsistency this phase's own tests caught between a stale import-time AdapterStatus and a live check; list_enabled_sources()/list_unavailable_sources() now bucket by final_status so a restricted board with an available provider moves into the GUI's Available list)

web/app.js (renderSourceStatus() rewritten to branch on final_status via a new sourceStatusLine() helper -- 'Available via Search Provider — <Provider>' / 'Search provider not configured / Configure a search API to enable discovery.' -- plus a new Search Provider Status summary line; the old reason-code-based shortReason() lookup table removed entirely, not left dangling)

web/dashboard.html (fetches /api/settings/search-providers alongside the dashboard call and passes it to renderSourceStatus() for the new summary line; removed the now-redundant standalone Search Provider Settings button in favor of the one rendered inside the sources block)

web/search_new.html (checkbox list now built from board-level sources.enabled -- shows a friendly 'LINKEDIN (via Search Provider: Serper)' label while submitting the correct internal LINKEDIN_SEARCH registry key as the checkbox value; the user never manually picks a provider)

api/main.py (4 new short-path aliases matching Part 6 exactly: GET /api/search-providers, POST /api/search-providers/{provider}/test|enable|disable -- delegate to the same api/search_provider_settings_api.py logic the existing /api/settings/search-providers/* routes already use, zero duplicate implementation)
